subject.title: [Security] Privilege escalation via mock environment overrides in testing framework

question: Can untrusted contributor-controlled code invoke this helper in an OpenClaw CI job that also receives real credentials or privileged tokens?
rationale: The answer determines whether this is an actual CI authorization boundary requiring remediation or expected behavior inside trusted test code; the issue does not identify enough workflow evidence to decide safely.

options.title: Request boundary proof
options.body: Ask for the exact workflow, trigger, fork trust level, available secret names, helper call path, and a redacted current-main reproduction before accepting a security fix.

options.title: Close as test-only behavior
options.body: If no credential-bearing workflow runs untrusted code through this helper, close the report under the documented test-harness security scope and invite private resubmission with concrete boundary evidence.

recommendation.title: Request boundary proof
recommendation.body: Ask for the exact workflow, trigger, fork trust level, available secret names, helper call path, and a redacted current-main reproduction before accepting a security fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work is the closest available history signal for environment inheritance and security-boundary hardening.
